newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-AUSTRALIA CHALLENGES FOR AMERICA'S CUP.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-AUSTRALIA CHALLENGES FOR AMERICA'S CUP.

text.p: Australia's most successful ocean yachtsman Syd Fischer on Tuesday announced he would challenge for the America's Cup in New Zealand in 2000.
The challenge will be Fischer's fifth bid to win the America's Cup -- equalling the record of Cup campaigns set by British yachtsman Sir Thomas Lipton in the 1920s and 1930s.

Fischer's announcement comes one day before entries close and leaves him the only Australian entrant after former challenger Iain Murray last week scrapped his plans to bid for the Cup in Auckland due to costs.
Fischer lodged his challenge through the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia (CYCA) in Sydney, the country's premier ocean racing yacht club which annually stages the Sydney-to-Hobart.
"I believe this will be a great campaign for Australia," Fischer told reporters.
"I think there is a lot of interest in the America's Cup because it is a symbol of the yachting prowess of the country that holds it. It is still the greatest yachting trophy."

Fischer maintained his customary silence on the expense of his America's Cup campaign. His 1995 campaign in San Diego was considerably smaller than that of other challengers who spent up to US$40 million in pursuit of the Cup.
His Sydney 95 yacht was eliminated early in the flukey conditions off San Diego in 1995 but Fischer was confident fresher conditions in Auckland would suit his 2000 challenge.
The lack of other Australia challengers would also be to his advantage in gathering sponsorship and crew members, he said.

"That will assist us to build up the best sailors and should help us avoid confusion with sponsors," said Fischer, rejecting suggestions the Sydney 2000 Olympics sponsorship drive would hinder his search for corporate sponsors.
Fischer first challenged for the America's Cup at Newport, Rhode Island, in 1983, and then in 1987 and 1992 before 1995.

He plans to use his Sydney 95 yacht to start his 2000 campaign and will build one new International America's Cup-class yacht. Campaigning for the Cup in Auckland will run from October 1999 to February 2000.
The Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron's Team New Zealand, with a black boat nicknamed "Black Magic", won the America's Cup from the San Diego Yacht Club in May 1995.
Australia first challenged for the America's Cup in 1962 with the yacht Gretel and eventually won the Cup in 1983 with Australia II sailed by John Bertrand.

Australia's 1995 campaign was hampered when Bertrand's oneAustralia, regarded as the fastest yacht in the regatta, broke in two and sank, leaving Bertrand to sail the semifinals and final of the challengers' series in a slower boat.

Fischer is Australia's most successful ocean yachtsman. His successes include two line honours victories in the Sydney-to-Hobart and the 1969 Fastnet Race. In 1996 he led an Australia team to victory in the Kenwood Cup in Hawaii.
He has also been captain of the Australian Admiral's Cup team five times, winning in 1979, and will lead Australia again later this year.
